text: The World of Warcraft: Warlords of Draenor Digital Deluxe Edition (WoD DDE for short) includes a full digital copy of Warlords of Draenor, as well as in-game content to aid you in your heroic adventures across . The digital deluxe version essentially provides the in-game rewards of the Collector's Edition at a reduced cost, but without the out-of-game items (such as the soundtrack and the art book). This deluxe edition is no longer available for purchase since July 11, 2021. Unlike the mounts and pets from the Legion and Battle for Azeroth deluxe editions, the mount and pet from this deluxe haven't been made available since.

World of Warcraft: Looking for Group is a documentary film created for the 10th anniversary of World of Warcraft that delves into the history of the game's development. It includes many of the developers and explores WoW's impact on the community worldwide. It premiered at BlizzCon on 8 November 2014.

It contains stunning artworks, crosswords, match-ups, quizzes, comics, and word puzzle. Comics Gnome vs Goblin and Warcraft Saga are also included.

World of Warcraft: Legion is the sixth expansion for World of Warcraft. It was announced at Gamescom on 6 August 2015 and released on 30 August 2016, selling 3.3 million copies by the end of launch day. The expansion's alpha went live on 23 November 2015, then concluded on 10 May 2016 in order for the beta to start two days later. The pre-expansion patch, patch 7.0.3, was released on July 19, 2016. Legion comes in three versions: Standard Edition, Digital Deluxe Edition and Collector's Edition.
World of Warcraft: Illidan is a World of Warcraft novel by William King. The book is a close look at Illidan as a character and what makes him who he is.

The World of Warcraft: Ultimate Visual Guide, Updated and Expanded is an official Warcraft timeline book of events, locations, and characters that have made up the game since its release. It contains stunning artwork and even some previously unknown lore. It is the successor of the first Ultimate Visual Guide.
World of Warcraft: Legion - Deluxe Hardcover Sketchbook is an official artbook.
The World of Warcraft: Legion Collector's Edition is the collector's edition of Legion.

The World of Warcraft: Legion Digital Deluxe Edition includes a full digital copy of Legion, as well as in-game content to aid you in your heroic adventures across the Broken Isles. The digital deluxe version provides the in-game rewards of the Collector's Edition at a reduced cost, but without the out-of-game items (such as the soundtrack and the art book). This deluxe edition is no longer available for purchase since July 11, 2021. The mount and pet were made available for purchase separately.

World of Warcraft: Chronicle Volume 2 is the second installment of the World of Warcraft: Chronicle series. It covers the history of Draenor and the events of the First and Second Wars, and ends with Draenor's destruction.

The World of Warcraft: Legion Companion App was announced at PAX West on September 3, 2016 and released on September 6, 2016. It is a free mobile phone application for iOS and Android that allows the player to manage their Class Hall Missions while away from their computer. As part of the announcement on June 22, 2018 of an ending of support for World of Warcraft Mobile Armory, it was stated that the Legion Companion App would be re-purposed in the future as a new "World of Warcraft Companion App". This app was superseded on August 13, 2018 as the World of Warcraft: Companion App.
World of Warcraft: An Adult Coloring Book is an adult artbook, published by Blizzard Publishing on December 13, 2016.

World quests were introduced in Legion as an expansion of the traditional daily quest system of previous expansions. World quests rotate on different times across the areas they are active, and they involve greatly varying objectives. All players in the same region will have the same set of world quests at any particular time, though some are only visible with certain professions or by progressing through specific quests in an area.

World of Warcraft: Chronicle Volume 3 is the third and final installment of the World of Warcraft: Chronicle series. It covers the events of Warcraft III up through World of Warcraft: Cataclysm. Like the previous volume, Volume 3 takes a pretty high level approach to the events.

World of Warcraft: Classic (later rebranded Classic Era) is a recreation of "vanilla WoW" as a server option for World of Warcraft announced at BlizzCon 2017. The goal of Classic is to let players experience World of Warcraft as close as possible to what it was before The Burning Crusade. With the addition of World of Warcraft: Burning Crusade Classic, existing characters must choose whether to stay in Classic or move on to the expansion. A character can be activated for use in both versions via the Activate Clone service, which creates a copy of the character as they were when the expansion choice was made. The World of Warcraft Diary is a book about the development of World of Warcraft. Though not licensed by Blizzard, the book was written by World of Warcraft's first Level Designer, Johnathan Staats. After his time at Blizzard, Staats compiled a great number of notes that he took all throughout the development of the game into a book, with the approval of the company. This project was funded through a Kickstarter, which was fully backed up within 10 minutes of its launch, August 28, 2018. The book provides a unique, detailed look into the development of World of Warcraft, from conceptualizing to implementing. Note that the other questgivers will not award the Twilight Cache - they award an Obsidian Cache (item) instead. After completing The Shadow of His Wings, the membership is also sold by Dealer Vexil at the Smoldering Perch in the Waking Shores for . Using the item will cause the player to become a Worldbreaker and allows for Magmote drops from hostiles in and around the citadel. The buff lasts for 48 hours of in-game time, or until death, whichever comes first.

The Worldbreakers are a faction of black dragonkin found in the Smoldering Perch in the Waking Shores. Originally known as the "Warders of the Earth" and "Children of the Earth", they have been converted by Cygenoth into believing the prophecies of the Twilight's Hammer; hoping to bring about the Hour of Twilight. After Cygenoth's death, who was revealed to actually be a Twilight's Hammer ogre in disguise, several of his cohorts continued his ruse. World of Warcraft: The War Within (shortened TWW) is the tenth expansion for World of Warcraft, and the start of the Worldsoul Saga story arc. It is set primarily in Khaz Algar, a large region beneath the surface of Azeroth. The expansion was officially announced at BlizzCon on November 3, 2023 alongside World of Warcraft: Cataclysm Classic, and was released on August 26, 2024 . The Worldsoul Saga will be continued in later expansions, World of Warcraft: Midnight and World of Warcraft: The Last Titan.

World of Warcraft: The Voices Within is a short story anthology serving as a tie-in to the events of The War Within. It was released on December 31, 2024.

The World of Warcraft Soundtrack was composed and arranged by Jason Hayes, Tracy W. Bush, Derek Duke and Glenn Stafford. It was released on November 23, 2004, together with the collector's edition of the game. The soundtrack can also be purchased via the Blizzard Store, iTunes or Amazon. It features most of the compositions featured in the original release of the game. Many of the earlier Warcraft game soundtracks are referenced in the composition of the score. Stylistically, the soundtrack is closer to that of Warcraft III than any of the previous titles, which may be due to the fact that the same man, Jason Hayes, was the major contributor to both soundtracks. .]] Wraiths are spirit-beings who are similar to ghosts, banshees, and shades in that they are the spectral remains of a once-living person. Wraiths appear to be of either elven or human origin most of the time. Some trolls in Zul'Gurub and the Temple of Atal'Hakkar manifest as wraiths before they die. Wraiths appear as translucent shapes with a roughly humanoid shape, although notably missing legs, and chains symbolically binding them to this life. They are typically either bluish or purple, and when they are killed, all that is left is a small orb. Wound Poison is a poison that is purchased from a poison vendor and applied to a rogue's weapons. Every time the rogue hits with the weapon, there is a chance (modified by the speed of the weapon) of the victim being poisoned for 15 seconds. The poison will reduce all healing effects on the victim by 25%. The effect cannot stack.

Worms are a type of invertebrate found on Azeroth, Outland, Draenor, and the Elemental Plane. They have long, tubular bodies, ranging in length from a few inches to several feet or more. Many species are segmented and have few or no limbs. Worms generally live underground, in deserts, or in places with plenty of carrion. In World of Warcraft, worms tend to be classified as beasts or critters. Some species are skinnable, while others are not. Worm items are often useful as fishing bait, and some worms can be kept as companions.

__NOTOC__ Worn Dragonscales are skinned from the bodies of Dragonkin. Even though these scales aren't pristine and shiny, these tough scales can be used for crafting armor. No dragonkin mobs have a particularly high drop rate, so collecting large stacks requires a considerable amount of grinding. Dustwallow Marsh is reputedly a good place to hunt for them. You can also occasionally find a stash of dragonscales in Knot Thimblejack's Cache in Dire Maul.

Every baby worm dreams of being a gladiator in the worm arena, where burly worms battle it out to eat sheep, grow, and squish their adversaries. Wormhead is a worm who fights in a worm arena in the official Blizzard scenario map for Warcraft III called Worm War. The worm is fed sheep and pigs from which it produces "segments" which follow it. These segments are covered in spikes. Fire elementals are also kept in the arena which might harm the worm. The worm can eat fire elementals with the help of a special item, and each fire elemental is worth 5 more segments.

The Woven Wand was created as a bond of friendship between Thule Ravenclaw, Bethor Iceshard and Gunther Arcanus, when they were apprentice magi in Dalaran. The bond was sundered when Ravenclaw sold his soul to the Lich King, while Bethor and Gunther were both struck down by the plague. Thule grew to despise the wand, but found that he could not part with it. So he took it with him, and placed it in a hidden niche within Fenris Keep in Silverpine Forest, where Ravenclaw made his lair. The wand was rediscovered after agents of the Horde attacked Fenris Keep and were led to the hidden alcove by the still-talking head of Alaric, Ravenclaw's former head servant. WowJutsu is a site to track guild progression. It uses the Armory's automatically updated profiles to tally how far a guild has progressed for all content post-Burning Crusade. This is accomplished by tracking the highest-level item worn by members of a particular guild when they log out, which means, for instance, a guild first kill in which the loot is disenchanted requires one member of the guild (probably the disenchanter) to equip an item and log out at least once in order for the progression to be tallied. WoWuction is an online resource which tracks and processes WoW Auction House data using Blizzard API. It was released a few months after Blizzard announced the API (mid 2011) which exposes WoW auction house data - encouraging many similar projects. WoWuction covers all realms in the EU and US regions and attempts to provide quick info on current AH opportunities, as well as many statistical and historical insights into global and realm economy.
